papers.title: Decellularized extracellular matrix-based bio-ink with enhanced 3D printability and mechanical properties.
papers.abstract: Recently, decellularized extracellular matrix-based bio-ink (dECM bio-ink) derived from animal organs is attracting attention because of its excellent biocompatibility. However, its poor 3D printability and weak mechanical properties remain a challenge. Here, we developed a new dECM bio-ink with enhanced 3D printability and mechanical properties. dECM micro-particles of about 13.4 μm in size were prepared by decellularizing a porcine liver followed by freeze-milling. The new bio-ink, named as dECM powder-based bio-ink (dECM pBio-ink), was prepared by loading the dECM micro-particles into a gelatin mixture. The usefulness of the dECM pBio-ink was evaluated by assessing its mechanical properties, printability, and cytocompatibility. The results showed that its mechanical properties and 3D printability were greatly improved. Its elastic modulus increased by up to 9.17 times that of the conventional dECM bio-ink. Micro-patterns with living cells were successfully achieved with 93% cell viability. Above all, the new bio-ink showed superior performance in stacking of layers for 3D printing, whereas the conventional bio-ink could not maintain its shape. Finally, we demonstrated that the dECM pBio-ink possessed comparable cytocompatibility with the conventional dECM bio-ink through in vitro tests with endothelial cells and primary mouse hepatocytes.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文专注于生物墨水材料性能提升，完全没有涉及人工智能或机器学习方法。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not integrate any AI or machine learning into the bioprinting workflow, lacks autonomous decision-making, and has no computational model validation.

summary_zh.motivation: 改善脱细胞外基质生物墨水的打印性和力学强度
summary_zh.method: 制备猪肝脏脱细胞粉末并混入明胶形成新型生物墨水
summary_zh.result: 弹性模量提升9.17倍，微图案细胞活性93%
summary_zh.validation: 力学测试和细胞培养验证

summary_en.motivation: To overcome the poor printability and weak mechanical properties of decellularized extracellular matrix-based bio-inks.
summary_en.method: Decellularized porcine liver micro-particles (13.4 μm) were loaded into a gelatin mixture to form a powder-based bio-ink.
summary_en.result: The bio-ink exhibited up to 9.17 times higher elastic modulus and achieved 93% cell viability in micro-patterns.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing (elastic modulus) and in vitro cytocompatibility assays with endothelial cells and hepatocytes.

papers.title: Zirconia versus titanium in dentistry: A review.
papers.abstract: This review scientifically compares the properties of zirconia and titanium, but does not identify the best among them as an implant material. Surface treatment and modification to improve tissue bonding and inhibit bacterial adhesion are not considered in this review. The mechanical properties of titanium are superior to those of zirconia; some studies have shown that zirconia can be used as a dental implant, especially as an abutment. Extensive surface treatment research is ongoing to inhibit bacterial adhesion and improve osseointegration and soft tissue adhesion phenomena which make it difficult to evaluate properties of the materials themselves without surface treatment. Osseointegration of titanium is superior to that of zirconia itself without surface treatment; after surface treatment, both materials show comparable osseointegration. The surface morphology is more important for osseointegration than the surface composition. To inhibit bacterial adhesion, zirconia is superior to titanium, and hence, more suitable for abutments. Both materials show similar capability for soft tissue adhesion.
papers.first_author_affiliation: Institute of Biomaterials and Bioengineering, Tokyo Medical and Dental University.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该综述比较了钛和氧化锆在牙科种植体中的性能，但未涉及增材制造、多孔结构或疲劳测试，与用户的研究方向不直接相关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical review of zirconia vs titanium dental implant materials, with no additive manufacturing, no porous structure design, no LPBF fabrication, and no mechanical testing of printed implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较氧化锆和钛作为牙科种植体材料的性能优劣。
summary_zh.method: 文献综述，对比两种材料在力学、骨整合和抗菌方面的性质。
summary_zh.result: 钛的力学性能优于氧化锆，但氧化锆在抑制细菌粘附方面更优。
summary_zh.validation: 未涉及实验验证，仅基于文献总结。

summary_en.motivation: To compare the properties of zirconia and titanium for dental implant applications through a literature review.
summary_en.method: A review of mechanical properties, osseointegration, and bacterial adhesion of both materials without surface treatment.
summary_en.result: Titanium shows superior mechanical properties, while zirconia exhibits better bacterial adhesion inhibition, making it more suitable for abutments.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation was performed; findings are based on existing literature.
